analysis: The PR modifies only docs/developer/test.md, a developer test guide. Per the file_changes patch excerpt, the changes are the 'Last updated' date (line 3), a CI description edit saying all Mac jobs are routed (previously the 3 GPU shards ran on Blacksmith), and a note that a `required` lane keeps its fallback without asking while sizes are off. The excerpt is truncated, and those later hunks (head ~2056-2061) fall outside the supplied head text, which ends at line 927, so I could not examine them directly. I read the supplied head text in both units for security-relevant guidance. Test instructions use isolated state and synthetic credentials. They tell the reader never to use production cache roots or keys and never to overwrite a running provider's state. They keep DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE test runs on ephemeral or isolated keys, consistent with the T-041 cache posture. They also keep the production free-space checks, write limits and cleanup in force when DARKBLOOM_SSD_TEST_TMPDIR is used, and they reject symlink and relative paths. No production code, key custody, authorization, attestation or encryption behavior changes. No threat model assumption is invalidated. The CI change moving the GPU shards from Blacksmith to routed Mac runners alters CI infrastructure trust only in prose. The workflow files, runner configuration and job-size routing that would make this a real change (scripts/ci-tested-tree.py, the build.md job-sizes section, the CI workflows) are not in the supplied evidence, so I record that as an unverified contract rather than a finding. A reviewer of the workflow changes, if any exist in other batches, should confirm that the routed runners keep read-only permissions and that release workflows stay on literal Blacksmith runners, as the docs state. No findings.
